labs.title: Measurement, Rates & Error Lab
labs.task: Measure or estimate three real quantities, convert units, compute one unit rate, and compare a measured value with an accepted or reference value.

labs.title: Expression Structure Lab
labs.task: Create three algebraic expressions from short situations, label terms/coefficient/constant, evaluate them, simplify them, then factor a shared GCF where possible.

labs.title: Equation Balance Lab
labs.task: Model four balance situations with equations, solve each, verify by substitution, and rearrange one formula for a requested variable.

labs.title: Constraint & Tolerance Lab
labs.task: Model capacity, budget, and tolerance situations with inequalities and absolute value; graph the feasible sets on number lines.

labs.title: Function Machine Lab
labs.task: Build an input-output rule from a real or invented process, generate a table, state domain/range, test whether the relation is a function, and write a matching rule.

labs.title: Linear Data & Residual Lab
labs.task: Collect or use at least six paired observations, fit a reasonable line, calculate slope and two residuals, and discuss interpolation versus extrapolation.

labs.title: Systems Decision Lab
labs.task: Compare two cost or resource plans, solve their intersection algebraically, verify it, and add one inequality constraint to identify a feasible region.

labs.title: Growth, Decay & Sequences Lab
labs.task: Compare one additive pattern and one multiplicative pattern, generate tables, write explicit rules, and model a growth or decay scenario.

labs.title: Polynomial Area Lab
labs.task: Represent rectangular areas with polynomial products, expand them, reverse the process by factoring, and connect factors to possible dimensions or zeros.

labs.title: Parabola & Optimization Lab
labs.task: Investigate a quadratic model by locating vertex, axis, zeros, and discriminant, then interpret a maximum or minimum in context.

labs.title: Coordinate Geometry Survey Lab
labs.task: Plot four locations on a coordinate map, compute two distances, one midpoint, and two slopes, simplifying radicals when needed.

labs.title: Data, Finance & Evidence Lab
labs.task: Analyze a small data set and a financial scenario, then critique a sampling claim for possible bias.

labs.title: Model Validation Lab
labs.task: Choose a real question, define variables, build a model, test it against evidence, identify limits, and defend a conclusion.

projects.title: Household Plan Comparison
projects.task: Compare two realistic pricing plans, model each linearly, solve the break-even point, apply a budget constraint, and recommend a plan for at least two usage scenarios.

projects.title: Growth Story Investigation
projects.task: Compare linear and exponential models for a growth or decay story, explain which fits better, and evaluate the risk of long-range prediction.

projects.title: Design With Polynomials
projects.task: Design a small geometric object or layout whose dimensions produce polynomial expressions; expand, factor, graph a related quadratic, and calculate a coordinate distance used in the design.

projects.title: Data & Money Decision Report
projects.task: Use a small public, household, or simulated data set to make a financial or planning decision, using statistics and a growth model while discussing bias and uncertainty.

projects.title: Integrated Algebra I Capstone
projects.task: Investigate a meaningful real-world question using at least three Algebra I model types or representations, validate results, state assumptions and limitations, and present a defensible recommendation or conclusion.

completion_policy.labs: teacher/family may assign selectively; labs can be used for remediation evidence
completion_policy.projects: projects may supplement unit evidence; capstone is recommended before final certification
completion_policy.mastery: project or lab completion never silently overrides the 80% assessment mastery requirement
